fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled PDF bytes are loaded as a poppler document; malformed content streams and image masks are parsed from this input.

fine_trace.code: for (int i = 0; i < doc->pages(); i++) { poppler::page *p = doc->create_page(i); r.render_page(p); }
fine_trace.note: Each page is rendered via page_renderer, which drives SplashOutputDev and Gfx to process content streams including image masks and transparency groups.

fine_trace.code: beginTransparencyGroup(state, bbox, nullptr, false, false, false);
fine_trace.note: An image mask in the PDF triggers creation of a non-isolated transparency group; the original bitmap is saved as transpGroup->origBitmap.
For a non-isolated group, the original bitmap content is copied into the new transparency-group bitmap via blitTransparent; src is origBitmap and dest is the new bitmap.

In the splashModeMono8 case, the source row stride is computed using bitmap->rowSize instead of src->rowSize. When the source bitmap (origBitmap) has a smaller rowSize than the destination bitmap, the source pointer advances past the end of each source row, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read.
The inner loop reads from the miscalculated source pointer sp, reading out-of-bounds memory beyond the src bitmap data buffer, which is detected by AddressSanitizer as a heap-buffer-overflow.
